record.field: Ask about building brain models with TVBO, or discuss the field — the schema, simulation backends, connectomes, papers and methods. Post a Question when there is an answer to accept, a Discussion when there is not.

div.p: Questions about the schema, simulation backends, connectomes, the Experiment Builder or the Python package — and discussions about methods, papers and where TVBO should go next. Both live here; you pick which one you are posting.
Reading is open to everyone. To post, create an account and confirm your email address.
Every topic is one of two kinds, chosen when you post and changeable afterwards. Nothing else differs — same forum, same tags, same search.

ul.li: Question — there is a concrete answer. Replies are voted on and you mark the one that solved it, so the thread stays useful to the next person who hits the same wall.
Discussion — there is no single right answer. The thread stays open and nothing gets accepted.
How to express something in the TVBO schema (dynamics, couplings, integrators, observation models).
Choosing and configuring a simulation backend, and what each optional extra provides.
Connectomes, atlases and parcellations — loading, normalizing, exporting.
Using the Knowledge Graph, the Experiment Builder, the REST API or the Python package.
Errors and unexpected results, with enough detail to reproduce them.
Modeling approaches and their trade-offs.
Papers, datasets and methods relevant to whole-brain modeling.
Reproducibility, sharing and standards practice.
Feedback on TVBO — what is missing, what should change.
Introductions, and what you are working on.

div.h3: How to ask a good question

ul.li: Search first — the answer may already be here or in the platform guide.
One question per post, with a title that states the actual problem.
Include the model or experiment you are working from, the backend, and the TVBO version.
Paste the exact error, not a paraphrase. Code and tracebacks belong in code blocks.
Say what you expected and what happened instead.
Answer the question that was asked. Use a comment to request clarification.
Prefer a self-contained answer over a bare link — links rot, this archive should not.
If a question is a duplicate, link the original rather than answering twice.
Assume good faith and argue with the claim, not the person.
Cite sources for empirical claims, and disclose a conflict of interest when you have one.
No recruitment spam, no promotion unrelated to brain modeling.

div.p: Confirming your email address grants the karma needed to post and vote. Upvote what is useful and correct; on a question, the asker accepts the reply that solved the problem. Karma accumulates as your posts are upvoted and accepted, and unlocks editing and moderation abilities.
A brand-new account's first post is reviewed by a moderator before it appears — a spam gate, not a judgement on the post. Everything after that is published immediately.
